constraint_review: No grid electricity; solar energy only - met: 2.4 kWp PV + 5.12 kWh LiFePO4 + MPPT + DC chiller supplies 3.6 kWh/day holding + 2 kWh/day 200kg batch within 8.1 kWh/day PV yield with night on battery. Store about 1 tonne of fresh produce - met: 2-2.4 m 100 mm PU box with 2 racks and ~60 vented crates holds 1 tonne at 4-10 C in holding mode, with operational cap of 200 kg/day warm intake to stay inside sun/battery budget.
feedback: Concept works physically and is buildable - accept. Energy chain PV->MPPT->48V LiFePO4->DC vapor-compression chiller->insulated box is a closed load path; sense chain box air sensor->thermostat->chiller is a closed signal path. No conservation violation. Re-derived checks: conduction 0.22*25.6*30~169 W vs claimed 186 W plausible; steady thermal 376 W / COP 2.5 =150 W electric correct; 150W*24h=3.6 kWh/day correct; 2.4kWp yielding 8.1 kWh/day implies ~3.4 kWh/kWp/day plausible tropical; holding+batch 3.6+2.0=5.6 kWh 0.69 of yield correct; night 150W*14h=2.1 kWh 0.41 of 5.12 kWh correct; 5.12/3.6=1.42 days autonomy correct; full-tonne pull-down 1000*~3.6kJ/kgK*25K~90MJ~25 kWh thermal correct; 1 tonne*~3.5kJ/kgK*2K~7MJ~1.94 kWh buffer correct; wind 0.5*1.2*30^2=540 Pa correct, *~5.3 m2~2.86 kN correct vs >10 kN gravity, anchored; soil 2.5 kPa << typical 50-150 kPa capacity safe. Everyday scales: 150 W is a bulb, 3.6 kWh is small-household daily, 2.5 kPa is ~250 kg/m2 floor load very light, wind push ~300 kgf held by tonne mass. Buildable with purchasable parts: mono-Si panels, 48V 100Ah LiFePO4, 60A MPPT, PU sandwich panels, DC compressor, HDPE crates, steel angle, concrete - all ordinary cast/bolt/fit methods; sketches E25,E36,E49 show arrangement. Meeting facts: consensus after 4 cycles, 4x ready, no open objections; proposal stable, supports acceptance. Prior art ColdHubs 3-tonne solar+battery crates and Ecofrost 5-6 tonne 2.5-3.5 kW confirms regime; this is credible 1-tonne scale-down with explicit PV-battery sizing and separate PV rack vs roof-PV. Deviations noticed but acceptable: full-tonne warm pull-down needs ~10 kWh electric > daily surplus - cannot fast-chill 1 tonne at once, mitigated by 200 kg/day cap + no-batch cloudy rule, still meets store-1-tonne holding function; 1.42-day no-batch autonomy is short for long cloudy stretch, mitigated by sealed door + 1.94 kWh/2K produce buffer; 2.4 kWp/5 kWh is tight if infiltration/door openings/respiration higher - acknowledged as open question. Claims resting on no evidence: 60-crate count for 1 tonne - E35 calc failed and never redone, no successful volume/mass calc; $1k-10k cost class - no cost search; assumed_constraints citing C2/C4/C8 - invalid IDs with empty evidence_ids; COP 2.5 assumed - E20-E22 prove DC compressors exist but no datasheet COP value quoted; door-opening air exchange and varied produce respiration - no simulation. None break working principle at concept stage. Remaining work (not blocking): compute crate fill mass/volume for target crops, verify chiller datasheet COP at 40C ambient, add infiltration estimate for cooperative door cycles, confirm wire gauge/fusing for 8.33 A 48V DC and MPPT rating.
